ei.title: Language That Distances Animals from Us
ei.subject: 9월_2023 고1 모의고사
ei.lesson: Language That Distances Animals from Us

fullPassage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders — employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task — like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds — they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.

questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans (A)[downplay / highlight] similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the (B)[best / worst] offenders — employing technical language to (C)[connect / distance] the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task — like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds — they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
① downplay — worst — distance: 원문 일치 ←정답
② highlight(부각하다) — worst — distance: (A) 오답. 우위를 지키려면 유사성을 '경시(downplay)'해야 함
③ downplay — best — distance: (B) 오답. 과학자들이 '최악의(worst)' 위반자일 수 있음
④ downplay — worst — connect: (C) 오답. 전문 용어로 동물을 우리와 '거리 두기(distance)'

questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders — employing (A)[technical / casual] language to distance the other animals from us. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task — like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds — they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
① casual(가벼운) — interpret — define: (A) 오답. 동물을 멀리하려 '전문(technical)' 용어 사용
② technical — interpret — define: 원문 일치 ←정답
③ technical — ignore — define: (B) 오답. 증거를 '해석(interpret)'함
④ technical — interpret — undermine: (C) 오답. 인간성을 '정의(define)'한다고 여겨지는 도구 제작

questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders — employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task — like how certain bird species can remember the (A)[precise / vague] locations of thousands of seeds — they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to (B)[strengthen / disempower] animals, the way we (C)[discover / invent] words to maintain our spot at the top.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
① vague(모호한) — disempower — invent: (A) 오답. 씨앗의 '정확한(precise)' 위치를 기억
② precise — strengthen — invent: (B) 오답. 언어로 동물을 '무력화(disempower)'
③ precise — disempower — invent: 원문 일치 ←정답
④ precise — disempower — discover: (C) 오답. 우위를 지키려 단어를 '지어냄(invent)'

questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay ①<u>similarities</u> between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "favorite affiliation partners"; they interpret ③<u>evidence</u> showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a ④<u>physical</u> task — like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds — they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
① similarities: 우리와 동물의 '유사성' — 적절
② worst: 과학자가 '최악의' 위반자일 수 있음 — 적절
③ evidence: 까마귀·침팬지가 도구를 만든다는 '증거' — 적절
④ physical(신체적) → cognitive(인지적): 씨앗 위치를 기억하는 것은 '인지적' 과제이므로 physical은 부적절 ←정답

The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we ④<u>invent</u> words to maintain our spot at the top.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
① exaggerate(과장하다) → downplay(경시하다): 우위를 지키려면 유사성을 '경시'해야 하므로 exaggerate는 부적절 ←정답
② technical: 동물을 멀리하는 '전문' 용어 — 적절
③ interpret: 증거를 '해석'함 — 적절
④ invent: 우위를 지키려 단어를 '지어냄' — 적절

✅ ① mouth-to-mouth contact: 과학자들이 침팬지의 '입맞춤(kissing)'을 차가운 전문 용어로 바꿔 부른다는 맥락
❌ ② a sign of affection(애정의 표시): 따뜻한 표현이라 전문 용어화 맥락과 반대
❌ ③ social bonding(사회적 유대): kissing의 직접 대체어로 부적합
❌ ④ a playful greeting(장난스러운 인사): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: kissing → mouth-to-mouth contact: 따뜻한 말을 건조한 전문 용어로 대체

questions.passage: The famous primatologist Frans de Waal, of Emory University, says humans downplay similarities between us and other animals as a way of maintaining our spot at the top of our imaginary ladder. Scientists, de Waal points out, can be some of the worst offenders — employing technical language to distance the other animals from us. They call "kissing" in chimps "mouth-to-mouth contact"; they call "friends" between primates "__________"; they interpret evidence showing that crows and chimps can make tools as being somehow qualitatively different from the kind of toolmaking said to define humanity. If an animal can beat us at a cognitive task — like how certain bird species can remember the precise locations of thousands of seeds — they write it off as instinct, not intelligence. This and so many more tricks of language are what de Waal has termed "linguistic castration." The way we use our tongues to disempower animals, the way we invent words to maintain our spot at the top.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:

❌ ① close family members(가까운 가족): friends의 대체어로 부적합
❌ ③ natural companions(자연스러운 동반자): 따뜻한 표현이라 부적합
❌ ④ lifelong mates(평생의 짝): 문맥과 무관
